name: sources
description: Bordered card listing 1–N citation chips for a RAG response. Re-uses Citation per row inside a Radix Collapsible so consumers can collapse the list when the response references many sources.

props.name: sources
props.description: Array of `SourceRef` objects ({ title: string; url?: string; page?: number }). Each becomes a Citation chip.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.description: Whether the list is expanded by default.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional CSS classes on the root.

examples.title: RAG response sources
examples.description: Three retrieved sources for a question about auth.

examples.title: Streamed via <sources> markdown element
examples.description: Render an LLM response that emits <sources data='[…]' /> via the Markdown slot wiring.

ai.whenToUse: At the bottom of a RAG-style assistant response, listing every source the model cited. Pair with InlineCitation in the body text so the inline refs and the bottom-of-card list reference the same sources by index.
ai.whenNotToUse: Don't use for a single-source attribution (drop in a plain Citation). Don't use as navigation — Sources is reference-only; for query history use a sidebar or breadcrumb.
commonMistakes: Passing strings instead of `{ title, url? }` objects in the `sources` array
Composing inline citations with `Citation` (block-level) when `InlineCitation` (inline + hover popover) is the right choice
Setting `defaultOpen={false}` on a chat surface — users miss provenance information by default
Embedding raw URLs as titles (use the source's display name; URL hostname is a fallback Citation already provides)
ai.accessibilityNotes: Wraps Radix Collapsible — the trigger is a real <button> with aria-expanded; content gets aria-hidden when closed. Each Citation chip is keyboard-focusable when its url is set.
